descriptionChirho: A masculine noun denoting a hole, opening, or cavity in a surface or structure. Used of a hole bored in the lid of a chest for collecting temple offerings (2 Kgs 12:10), a hole in the wall of the temple through which Ezekiel looked in vision (Ezek 8:7), the holes or caves in which the Israelites hid from the Philistines (1 Sam 14:11), the holes or dens where creatures dwell (Job 30:6), the opening in a door through which the beloved thrust his hand (Song 5:4), the eye sockets in which flesh wastes away in eschatological plague (Zech 14:12), and the dens of Nahum's lion metaphor (Nah 2:12). The basic sense is any aperture or hollow space, whether natural or man-made.
